Monodromy of the

Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov Equations

The purpose of this chapter is twofold:

(i) For any complex Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ and any invariant symmetric 2-tensor $t\in\mathfrak{g}\otimes\mathfrak{g}$ , construct a quantum enveloping algebra $A_{\mathfrak{g},t}$ for $\mathfrak{g}$ whose canonical 2-tensor is $t.$

## XIX.1 Connections

We assume some standard knowledge of differential geometry. Let us nevertheless recall a few facts. For more details, the reader may consult [KN63].

Let X be a complex analytic variety of dimension n and p : E $\to$ X be a complex analytic vector bundle of rank d over X. If x is a point of X, we denote by $F_{x}$ the fibre at x: $F_{x}=p^{-1}(x).$ A connection on E is a linear map $\nabla$ from the space $\Gamma(X,E)$ of sections of the vector bundle E into the space $\Omega^{1}(X,E)$ of differential 1-forms with values in E such that for any section s and any complex analytic function f on X we have

$$
\nabla (f s) = (d f) s + f \nabla (s).
$$

(1.1)

If $\nabla_{1}$ and $\nabla_{2}$ are two connections on E, then the difference $\nabla_{1}-\nabla_{2}$ is $\mathcal{O}(X)$ -linear, where $\mathcal{O}(X)$ is the ring of complex analytic functions on X. Locally, we can write a section s in the form

$$
s = f _ {1} e _ {1} + \dots + f _ {d} e _ {d}
$$

(1.2)

where $f_{1},\dots,f_{d}$ are complex analytic functions on X and $\{e_{1},\dots,e_{d}\}$ is a basis of the fibre. Any connection $\nabla$ on E can be written locally as

$$
\nabla s = d s - \Gamma s
$$

(1.3)

where $d$ is the de Rham differential and $\Gamma$ is a differential 1-form on $X$ with values in the endomorphism ring of $E.$

A section s of the bundle is horizontal for the connection $\nabla$ if $\nabla s=0$ i.e., if locally s is a solution of the system

$$
d s = \Gamma s.
$$
